correctness.rationale: For t>=1 the refractory rule makes E_{t-1} disjoint from E_{t+1}. Every excited vertex at t has at least theta neighbors in E_{t-1} and so at most Delta-theta neighbors in E_{t+1}; counting edges E_t--E_{t+1} gives theta e_{t+1}<=(Delta-theta)e_t. Initially e1<=floor(Delta*n/(Delta+theta)), so the integer excitation count vanishes once the real geometric envelope is <1, with one final refractory-clearance step. For theta=Delta, e2=0 and total rest by time three. Layered bipartite predecessor-successor graphs with sizes |L_h|=1, |L_{h-1}|=theta, |L_j|=ceil(theta |L_{j+1}|/(Delta-theta)) and modular adjacency realize one travelling excited front per step and have maximum degree Delta; total vertices grow as (theta/(Delta-theta))^h, giving sharp logarithmic worst-time coefficient. Independently verified all modular predecessor degree bounds for four parameter pairs, including (3,2),(5,3),(7,4),(8,5).
